source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion: Go through the facility log for the day to check test times. 3. Review the test strips and compare the test results to the facility log. 4. Assess the facility log: Record the failure time and the correction time (not chemical additions or when the system goes free chlorine). 5. Determine what to report. 6. Document the failure and the corrective actions taken using the failure report. The first thing to do when any water quality concerns are detected is to check the inspection records for code violations that might contribute to water-quality problems. Download the Inspection Records Quick Reference Chart for a listing of common violations. DO NOT USE THE INSPECTOR COMMENT SECTION TO RECORD WATER QUALITY VIOLATIONS OR CORRECTIVE ACTIONS. INSPECTOR COMMENTS SHOULD PROVIDE THE DETAILS OF ANY VIOLATIONS, NOT THE CHEMICAL LEVELS. COMMUNICATE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND WATER CHEMISTRY DETAILS USING THE CORRECTIVE ACTION COMMENT SECTION
